name: SparkFun Electronics
old_description: Since 2003, SparkFun has been helping turn ideas into reality – whether you’re creating a smart weather station, exploring the frontier of machine learning, building a robot for school or prototyping your first (or tenth) product. No matter your vision or skill level, our open source components, resources and online tutorials are designed to broaden access to innovative technology and make the road to a finished project shorter.
about:
Founded in 2003 in Niwot, Colorado, SparkFun Electronics began as an open-source hardware company aimed at making electronics accessible to engineers, hobbyists, and educators. The company operates from its headquarters in the Boulder area, where it designs and manufactures a wide range of development boards, sensors, and kits under its own brand.

SparkFun develops and sells open-source electronic components, including microcontroller boards, environmental sensors, RFID modules, and wireless communication devices. It also operates a custom kit service that assembles tailored component packages for workshops, classrooms, and virtual learning programs. A subsidiary, SparkPNT, focuses on high-precision positioning, navigation, and timing products built to be durable, future-proof, and repairable. The company employs approximately 140 people and maintains an extensive catalog of both proprietary and third‑party components.

Customers span education, professional engineering, hobbyist, and product‑development sectors. SparkFun supplies components for AI robotics projects using NVIDIA Jetson modules, high‑precision GPS designs with u‑blox receivers, DIY biometric monitors, and community hackathons. Its distributor and reseller program extends volume pricing to partners, while the Qwiic solderless ecosystem enables rapid prototyping across processor and function boards.

The company emphasizes open‑source design, comprehensive documentation, and tutorials to lower barriers to emerging technology. Its stated mission is to provide hardware, services, and resources that make new technology easy to use, with products designed for durability and repairability.

old_description: At Spartan Auto parts, we understand the passion behind every restoration project. about:
Based in Inman, South Carolina, Spartan Auto & Heavy Truck Parts has served the automotive aftermarket for approximately 20 years. The company operates as a privately held distributor of used and OEM components for passenger vehicles and heavy trucks.

The business maintains an inventory of over 100,000 individual parts, ranging from mechanical components to body panels, and fulfills orders through its own e-commerce site and an eBay storefront. Its knowledgeable staff assists customers with part identification and offers price matching on comparable listings. Orders shipped to the lower 48 states typically arrive within one to five business days.

Customers include professional repair shops, fleet operators, and individual enthusiasts undertaking restoration projects. The catalog covers both routine maintenance items and hard-to-find pieces for older automobiles and commercial trucks, supporting everything from daily driver repairs to full-frame restorations.

The company emphasizes its combination of extensive stock, OEM-quality parts, and responsive service as its primary differentiators, aiming to reduce downtime for shops and keep restoration projects on schedule. Competitive pricing and a willingness to negotiate on larger orders further distinguish its offering.

name: Specialized Switchgear Solutions LLC
old_description: , we specialize in the design, manufacturing, and service of high-quality switchgear solutions. From custom builds to maintenance and retrofits, we deliver reliable power distribution systems that keep your business running safely and efficiently.
about:
Specialized Switchgear Solutions LLC is based in Mansfield, Ohio. The company was formed by Rick Knox and Donald Smith after the February 2020 closure of PACS Switchgear, where both had spent decades advancing through roles in assembly, quality, field service, and management. Knox, a Six Sigma Blackbelt, had overseen manufacturing operations with up to 400 employees, while Smith led special projects and parts management. Their combined experience spans the full lifecycle of medium‑voltage switchgear.

The firm designs, manufactures, and services switchgear for power distribution systems. Its offerings include custom switchgear builds, maintenance programs, and retrofits of existing equipment. The shop handles custom component fabrication such as circuit breakers, switches, potential transformer drawers, and ground‑and‑test devices, and provides field installation and commissioning support. Spare‑parts management and on‑site technical service round out the portfolio.

Customers are typically industrial and utility operators that require reliable medium‑voltage power distribution. The company’s background in high‑volume project execution — over 500 projects in a five‑year period at PACS — informs its approach to custom orders and retrofit work, though specific client names are not disclosed.

The owners emphasize three pillars: safety built to the highest industry standards, precision engineering backed by tested quality assurance, and customer service that extends beyond delivery. Knox’s lean‑manufacturing drive and Smith’s field‑service expertise are cited as the foundation for delivering dependable, tailored solutions.

name: Specialty Plastics Inc.
old_description: Specialty Plastics Inc. is a custom plastic injection molder located in St. Peters, MO. Our core competency is tight tolerance plastic parts. For over 40 years, we have supplied high quality injection molded products and services to a wide array of business: medical instruments, automotive, healthcare, home appliances, sporting goods, electrical and many more. about:
Specialty Plastics Inc. was founded in 1980 in St. Peters, Missouri, as a custom plastic injection molder. The company began with a focus on tight-tolerance plastic parts and has operated continuously for over four decades.

Beyond injection molding, the company offers blow molding, thermoset molding, insert molding, and over molding, plus secondary operations such as hot stamping, pad printing, laser marking, sonic welding, milling, drilling, assembly, and custom packaging.

Specialty Plastics serves a broad industrial base including medical instruments, automotive, healthcare, home appliances, sporting goods, electrical, electronics, industrial equipment, motor manufacturing, toys, and leisure equipment. The company supports customers with kanban and just-in-time inventory programs, and ships daily to local accounts under those arrangements.

The business emphasizes a partnership model, citing its ISO 9001 certification, a quality lab equipped with a CMM, optical comparator, Keyence automated inspection, and color spectrometry, and a standard two-week lead time for production orders. Management is directly accessible, and the plant operates 24 hours a day, five days a week.

Customers range from independent repair shops and engine builders to industrial maintenance teams and performance enthusiasts. The product lineup serves the automotive aftermarket, heavy-duty diesel, and industrial engine sectors, with specific coverage for brands like Detroit Diesel, Honda, and a wide array of racing and performance manufacturers.

The firm emphasizes its century-long continuity in engine machining and its broad stock availability as key differentiators, positioning itself as a single source for both machine work and the parts needed to complete a build.

name: Spotted Owl Timber Inc.
old_description: Spotted Owl Timber, Inc. is located in Santa Fe, NM. We are a locally owned sawmill that was founded in 1991 by David Lindsey. David is a third generation sawmill owner and operator. He was born in New Mexico and grew up in the logging and sawmill industry. David opened Spotted Owl in 1991 with a small Woodmizer band mill and cut beams and lumber for the growing demand of southwestern style homes in Santa Fe and around Northern New Mexico.
about:
Spotted Owl Timber, Inc. operates a sawmill in Santa Fe, New Mexico. The company was founded in 1991 by David Lindsey, a third-generation sawmill operator born and raised in New Mexico’s logging industry. Lindsey launched the business with a small Woodmizer band mill to supply beams and lumber for the growing demand for southwestern-style homes in Santa Fe and northern New Mexico.

The sawmill produces natural, custom wood products from locally sourced softwood species — Ponderosa pine, white fir, Douglas fir, and Engelmann spruce. Using a larger Woodmizer thin-kerf band mill and additional equipment, the operation cuts beams, dimensional lumber, and custom profiles. The thin-kerf blade reduces waste and yields up to 30 percent more lumber per log compared with traditional circle saws. All material is harvested by independent local loggers and processed without added chemicals.

Customers include contractors, private homebuilders, and the general public throughout northern New Mexico. The company’s products are used primarily in residential construction and custom home projects that emphasize regional architectural styles.

Lindsey started Spotted Owl to meet a specific regional need for locally milled, natural wood suited to southwestern designs. The company highlights its sustainable sourcing, thin-kerf efficiency, and chemical-free processing as key differentiators.
